summary: Configured GRE-tap based traffic mirroring: node1 duplicates all IPv4/ARP traffic exchanged with node2 (both directions) onto a gretap tunnel terminating on node3, using tc clsact/flower/mirred on node1's eth0. Node3 sees full copies of node1<->node2 traffic on its local gretap1 interface while the original node1<->node2 traffic keeps flowing unmodified over the shared segment. Configuration was made persistent (systemd unit on node1, OpenRC local.d script on node3) and verified to survive a one-at-a-time restart of all three nodes.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 (SONiC-VS/Debian 13), node2 and node3 (Alpine 3.23) and confirmed all three share one flat L2 segment 10.100.121.0/24 via eth0 (node1 assigned 10.100.121.10/24 matching CLUSTER_HOSTS, node2 .11, node3 .12)
Captured a healthy baseline: node3's eth0 sees zero packets of node1<->node2 ping traffic (real learning-switch behavior, no mirroring by default)
Installed tcpdump/iproute2 (tc) on both Alpine nodes via apk
Created a gretap tunnel node1(10.100.121.10)<->node3(10.100.121.12) named gretap1 on both ends

On node1: added tc clsact qdisc on eth0 with ingress/egress flower filters matching IPv4 and ARP traffic to/from node2 (10.100.121.11), action mirred egress mirror dev gretap1, duplicating (not redirecting) matched frames to the tunnel

Verified mirroring works: node3's gretap1 captured full ICMP request/reply and ARP exchange between node1 and node2 with original addresses intact, while node1<->node2 ping showed 0% packet loss throughout

Persisted configuration: systemd oneshot service traffic-mirror.service (enabled) on node1 recreates the address/tunnel/tc rules at boot; OpenRC /etc/local.d/traffic-mirror.start (local service enabled at default runlevel) recreates gretap1 on node3
Captured boot_id and health baseline on all three nodes, then restarted node2, node3, and node1 one at a time via native reboot, polled until each came back, and proved changed boot_id on each
Post-restart on node1: confirmed traffic-mirror.service active, eth0 address, gretap1, and all four tc filters recreated automatically
Post-restart end-to-end re-verification: node3's gretap1 again captured node1<->node2 ARP/ICMP traffic while the direct ping between node1 and node2 remained at 0% packet loss

evidence.requirement: Baseline: node3 does not see node1<->node2 traffic before mirroring is configured
evidence.summary: tcpdump on node3 eth0 filtered for node1/node2 IPs captured 0 packets while node1 pinged node2 successfully

evidence.requirement: Topology confirmation: node1, node2, node3 share one L2 segment
evidence.summary: Interface/address inspection plus successful ping from node1's newly assigned 10.100.121.10 to node2 (.11) and node3 (.12) confirms a single shared /24 segment

evidence.requirement: Mirroring mechanism configured (gretap tunnel + tc mirred filters on node1)
evidence.summary: gretap1 created on node1 and node3; tc clsact qdisc and ingress/egress flower+mirred filters installed on node1's eth0 matching node2's IP and ARP

evidence.requirement: Node3 receives a copy of node1<->node2 traffic (pre-restart)
evidence.summary: tcpdump on node3's gretap1 captured the ICMP request/reply exchanged between 10.100.121.10 and 10.100.121.11 while node1's ping to node2 succeeded

evidence.requirement: Original node1<->node2 traffic keeps flowing as before (unaffected by mirroring)
evidence.summary: Direct ping from node1 to node2 shows 0% packet loss both right after enabling mirroring and after all restarts
systemd traffic-mirror.service enabled and validated active on node1; OpenRC local service enabled and start script installed on node3

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id captured, reboot acknowledged and connection reset observed, new boot_id confirmed (ed56cc7b -> 81b9a827) with uptime 0 min, eth0 address and connectivity to node1/node3 restored

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state including gretap1 mirror interface
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id captured, reboot acknowledged, new boot_id confirmed (0278f086 -> e02cf8c4) with uptime 0 min, local service started and gretap1 automatically recreated by /etc/local.d/traffic-mirror.start

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state including mirror service, tunnel and tc filters
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id captured, reboot acknowledged, new boot_id confirmed (8e8823ec -> 577fd210) with uptime 0 min, traffic-mirror.service active, eth0 address, gretap1 and all 4 tc ingress/egress filters recreated automatically

evidence.requirement: Post-restart end-to-end verification: mirroring and original traffic both fully recovered
evidence.summary: After all three restarts, node3's gretap1 again captured the ARP/ICMP exchange between node1 and node2, and the direct ping between node1 and node2 showed 0% packet loss
